answer: Work-slot deposit burn charges per slot, not per account. An agent locks 100 credits as an anchor, and five peers check the work; fake work burns it, honest work returns it. Taking 1,000 slots locks 100,000 credits, losing 100 per failure, so cost grows linearly and cannot be recycled. A public ledger mirrors every burn. No controller can hide a river of lost deposits behind one honest account. An honest agent pays once and keeps its full reward.
